step1_summary: Chief complaint: Acute central chest pressure (“feels like someone sitting on my chest”) that began a couple of hours ago while gardening and is still present.

Symptoms: • Onset: sudden during light activity (kneeling while gardening) • Duration: ongoing for ~2 h at time of call • Character: diffuse central pressure, radiates to left arm and shoulder • Associated: shortness of breath, nausea (no vomiting), diaphoresis, feeling of rapid heartbeat (likely stress-related) • No prior similar episodes.
Past medical history: Hypertension; no diabetes; cholesterol never checked.
Medications / allergies: Aspirin allergy (mild swelling); other meds not mentioned.
Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction at ≈60 y; mother ‘had some heart problems’.
Social history: Smokes 10 cigarettes/day for 15 y; drinks 7–8 pints beer/week; overweight; low physical activity; lives alone; restaurateur.
Vital signs / physical exam: Not formally measured; patient appears sweaty and short of breath on video.
Labs / imaging: None yet (ambulance en-route for ECG).

V: Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina / myocardial infarction): Classic pressure-type chest pain with arm radiation, diaphoresis, nausea, multiple CAD risk factors.
Aortic dissection: Sudden chest pain in hypertensive smoker could represent dissection, though description less typical.
Pulmonary embolism: Acute chest discomfort and dyspnoea; obesity and smoking are minor risk factors.
I: Acute pericarditis/myocarditis: Chest pain and dyspnoea can mimic ACS, but radiation pattern and risk factors less supportive.
Pneumonia (atypical): Chest discomfort with SOB and diaphoresis possible, but no cough/fever reported.
N: Mediastinal or lung mass compressing structures: Unlikely given abrupt onset but considered in chronic chest pain.
D: Degenerative cervical/thoracic spine disease with radicular pain to arm: Could cause shoulder/arm pain but not chest pressure + systemic symptoms.
Anaemia (deficiency) precipitating demand ischaemia: Could exacerbate cardiac pain.
I2: Cocaine or stimulant-induced vasospasm: Presents like ACS, but no substance use reported.
C: Congenital hypertrophic cardiomyopathy causing ischaemic pain: Usually presents earlier; no history.
A: Autoimmune pericarditis: Less likely given presentation.
T: Musculoskeletal chest wall strain while gardening: Diffuse ache possible but systemic features argue against.
E: Gastro-oesophageal reflux / oesophageal spasm: Can mimic chest pain but lacks diaphoresis & arm radiation.
Panic/anxiety attack: Sweating, palpitations and chest tightness could occur, but first episode in 60-y-o with strong CAD risks makes this less likely.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome (myocardial infarction or unstable angina)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic anginal features (pressure, left-arm radiation, diaphoresis, nausea, ongoing >20 min) in a 60-year-old man with multiple CAD risk factors make ACS the most probable diagnosis.
supporting_evidence: Risk factors: male ≥60 y, smoker, hypertension, overweight, positive family history of premature MI
Occurred with minimal exertion (garden kneeling) → supply–demand mismatch
opposing_evidence: No explicit jaw/neck pain, but not required

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Hypertension and smoking are risk factors; dissection can present with chest pain and arm symptoms. Must be ruled out rapidly because life-threatening.
opposing_evidence: Pain described as pressure rather than sudden ‘tearing’
No radiation to back, abdomen, or neurological deficits

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Acute SOB and chest discomfort may represent PE, though lacking pleuritic nature or clear risk factors such as recent immobility or DVT.
supporting_evidence: Obesity and smoking modestly increase risk
opposing_evidence: Chest pain not pleuritic; described as central pressure
No calf pain, recent surgery, long travel, oestrogen use
Prominent cardiac risk profile better fits ACS

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Can cause central chest pressure but typically related to meals/lying down and lacks diaphoresis or arm radiation.
opposing_evidence: Associated diaphoresis, nausea, SOB, arm radiation more typical of cardiac origin

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Palpitations and sweating could be anxiety, but first episode at 60 y with classic angina features and risk factors makes this less plausible.
opposing_evidence: Physical activity trigger, arm radiation, strong CAD risks
